title: Supabase MCP server enables agents to provision backend infrastructure
source_used: Supabase blog 'Build anything: Supabase from code, and an MCP server for your app' (supabase.com/blog/select-2026-build-anything); TechGig gave only two sentences
key_facts: Supabase announced the tools "today at Supabase Select"; its blog lists the post and the Select 2026 recap with date 2 Oct 2026.
New tools let a coding agent set up a backend from code: schema written as SQL files with the new pg-delta engine generating migrations, and project config kept in config.toml.
Local Supabase can run as native processes without Docker, one stack per directory; it is in alpha and off by default.
Supabase Compute runs long-lived services next to the database; it is in private alpha with a waitlist.
An app can now have its own MCP server, deployed inside its Supabase project, so a user's agent in Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor sees only what that user is allowed to see.
Supabase says an app's MCP server is separate from the official Supabase MCP server, which helps developers build their app.
TechGig's 14 Oct 2026 article says Supabase has introduced MCP server support for agents to provision and modify backend infrastructure; it re-reports the 2 Oct announcement.
quote_evidence: Today at Supabase Select, we announced new tools that let your coding agent set up your backend, test changes locally, and deploy the services behind your app.
Your app can now have its own MCP server, deployed inside the Supabase project you already have.
Your app's MCP server is separate from the official Supabase MCP server, which helps you build your app.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers get a route for AI agents to manage a backend from code and for their users' agents to work inside an app under each user's permissions.
notes: Stale and partly misframed: TechGig (14 Oct) presents this as new "MCP server support", but the announcement is from Supabase Select on 2 Oct 2026 and Supabase already had an official MCP server. The TechGig page gave only two sentences, so I wrote from Supabase's own blog. A lavx.hu rewrite claims Supabase is the "first major" backend-as-a-service to do this; I did not use that unverified claim.
